generatedBy: hand-authored for the last-segment buckets, then verified with git 2.54.0's `git check-ignore -v --no-index` (the deciding rule line, negation included) before this file was written
note: The same schema as gitignore-vectors.json, kept separate because those 34 cases are the matcher contract and these pin one property of the decision order: a last-segment bucket is a candidate source, never an answer, so a later matching rule still wins and a later bucket rule still beats an earlier one. The last three cases pin the other ordering property of the same machinery: a leading `**/` is normalised at parse time into the unanchored rule it means, so it keeps its position in the file and a later (or earlier) `!` rule still wins; each carries enough filler bucket rules that the last-segment bucket is built, so the bucket and the scan are both exercised. Every case here is decided by the last matching line of its single rule file.

the later of two bucket rules for one extension wins
the later of two different buckets wins
the earlier bucket rule wins when the later candidate fails
a narrower bucket negation still wins over the broader suffix

a normalised **/*.log rule is overridden by a later !keep.log
